title: Using LLMs as prompt modifier to avoid biases in AI image generators

bias_targets.methodology: Generating images from underspecified prompts (e.g., occupations, characteristics) and using Vision Language Models (VLMs) along with manual review to analyze the statistical distribution of male, female, and non-binary individuals.

Generating images using default, occupational, and characteristic prompts (e.g., 'thug', 'terrorist') and utilizing VLMs to classify the generated subjects into ethnic categories (Caucasian, African, Asian, Hispanic) to measure demographic deviation and stereotyping.
Using VLMs to automatically classify the age of generated people into 'young', 'middle-aged', and 'old' categories across various underspecified job prompts to evaluate age diversity.

Evaluating images generated from prompts specifying physical disabilities (e.g., 'a disabled doctor in a wheelchair', 'ballet dancer with a prosthetic leg') to observe whether the models correctly attribute the disability or incorrectly transfer it to secondary subjects (like a patient).

Generating images based on region-specific prompts (e.g., 'African house', 'Iraqi car', 'Ethiopian car') and qualitatively assessing the outputs for visual diversity, cultural appropriateness, and the mitigation of narrow regional stereotypes.
Prompting image generators for 'curvy' or 'plus-sized' models on a catwalk to evaluate whether the models adhere to skinny fashion stereotypes or successfully depict diverse body mass indexes.
